messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — HelioHealth escalated: they say audit logs for an API key rotation event on 2026-03-10 are missing from the Console. They've opened a Sev-2 ticket and want scope, timeline, and whether KMS/HSM or key material was involved.

alex_oncall: Thanks — can you paste their example query and result? I'll check the ingestion pipeline and shipper metrics.

maria_support: Customer ran: `GET /admin/audit_logs?org=heliohealth&from=2026-03-10T00:00Z&to=2026-03-11T00:00Z`
Response snippet:
```
{"logs": []}
```

chris_sec: I'm on it. Any recent deploys touching audit-forwarder or ES index aliases around that time?

alex_oncall: There was a deploy 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC that updated log-shipper to switch to the new index alias. Rollout was gradual. I saw a spike of shipper errors at ~02:20 UTC. Snippet from shipper:`ERROR bulk_index failed: 503 ServiceUnavailable (index=audit-2026-03 alias=audit-current)`.

auditbot: Alert: audit-forwarder failed to index ~1242 documents between 2026-03-10T02:18:00Z and 2026-03-10T02:35:00Z for alias `audit-2026-03`.

chris_sec: We need to know if this is isolated to HelioHealth. Run a rollup query by org for that window to see ingestion drops.

alex_oncall: Query I ran: `SELECT org, count(*) FROM audit_ingest WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-10T02:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-10T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY org;`
Results: HelioHealth: 0 (expected ~1200), MedicaCorp: 0 (expected ~950), SmallBizX: normal. So looks like a handful of orgs affected, not global.

sara_cs: HelioHealth is worried about whether customer data was exposed or lost — they provided sample audit entries they expect to see.

derek_legal: We need to confirm scope and impact before external notification. Two tracks: (1) determine whether logs were never ingested (availability) vs ingested and later deleted (integrity), and (2) determine if any personal data appeared in logs and if there's any sign of exfiltration. If it's strictly retention/availability, notify customer with a timeline and remediation steps. If personal data was exposed, we may have GDPR notification obligations — escalate immediately.

chris_sec: Early signs: shipper bulk requests returned 503s; the shipper has a local spool directory that should contain failed bulks. I suspect documents were queued locally and not lost. I'll attempt spool_replay to reindex. ETA for initial triage: ~2h. Also checking KMS logs for any unusual key access. Note: KMS rotations occurred 2026-03-09 but all rotations showed successful ops with normal access patterns. No immediate evidence of KMS compromise.

alex_oncall: Reindex command I'm running: `./spool_replay --index audit-2026-03 --range '2026-03-10T02:00:00Z/2026-03-10T03:00:00Z' --dry-run=false`
Progress: 35% (430/1242) so far, reindexing from spool.

maria_support: Draft customer message for HelioHealth: "We detected an ingestion issue that made audit logs inaccessible between 02:18-02:35 UTC on 2026-03-10. Our team is restoring the affected logs and investigating root cause. We will update within 4 hours with remediation status and scope." Approve before I send?

derek_legal: Approve — please adjust wording: replace "our team" with "Redwood Inference" and add: "At this time we have no evidence of data exfiltration." Also ask for any sample log IDs from the customer for cross-checking. We should avoid speculative language.

chris_sec: Agreed with Derek. Confirming KMS check in progress: I'm pulling key access logs from HSM/KMS for 2026-03-09..10 to confirm no anomalous access. Will post results in 3h.

sara_cs: I'll send the updated message to HelioHealth and request sample log IDs. Creating internal ticket: INC-4021 and linking to customer ticket. I'll CC legal and security.

alex_oncall: Reindex job finished: `Replayed 1242 docs -> indexed 1242 docs` per spool_replay output. Verifying presence via admin query now.

auditbot: Reindex complete: 1242 documents restored to `audit-2026-03` alias.

chris_sec: Post-recheck summary: scope impacted 6 orgs (including HelioHealth, MedicaCorp). Impact window: 2026-03-10T02:18:00Z to 2026-03-10T02:35:00Z. Root cause: log-shipper config change incorrectly mapped alias -> ES returned 503s which caused local spool buffering. No evidence of data loss or exfiltration; documents were restored from local spool. KMS/HSM checks show normal rotations and no anomalous access.

chris_sec: Remediations planned: rollback problematic alias mapping to prevent recurrence (owner: alex_oncall), add indexing-error circuit-breaker to stop rollouts if bulk indexing errors exceed thresholds (owner: eng-runtime), and add an automated detection alert to catch indexing drops by org (owner: chris_sec). Customer comms: maria_support/sara_cs will send final closure note with timeline and root cause. Legal will review wording before send.

maria_support: :thumbsup: Sending final update to HelioHealth now (CC Derek). Closing internal ticket after legal sign-off. Thanks everyone.
